anomalies.observed: On the FCC Peripherals sheet the PCA9685PW (U2) address pin A0 (pin 1) is strapped to +3.3V and the sheet annotation reads 'I2C address: 0x41'.
anomalies.expected: The specification's component table defines the PWM/servo driver as 'NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40', which requires A0 tied low. The drawing's 0x41 strap deviates from the intended address.

evidence.quote: U2 PCA9685PW ... A0 pin 1 -> +3.3V ... 'I2C address: 0x41' (FCC Peripherals sheet)
PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40

anomalies.impact: The 16-channel PWM/servo driver answers at 0x41 instead of the intended 0x40. Firmware built against the reference design addresses the PCA9685 at 0x40 on I2C2 and will not find the device, so the servo/PWM outputs do not operate. (Note: the schematic also places the INA219, which the spec lists at 0x40, on the same I2C2 bus, so the 0x41 strap is the only value in the spec-vs-drawing comparison that diverges — everywhere else, including the physically questionable TMP100 '0x4E', the drawing and the spec agree.)

parsed.summary: The schematic matches the specification on every part identity and stated value except the PCA9685 I2C address: the drawing straps A0 high (note 'I2C address: 0x41') whereas the spec's intended design is 0x40, a deviation that would leave the servo/PWM driver unaddressable by reference firmware.
